title: Serial commands
summary: Control the board by typing commands.
goal: Typing "on" turns the LED on pin 13 on and replies "LED ON"; typing "off" turns it off and replies "LED OFF".
brief:
Serial works both ways: you can send text to the board too. Each command arrives as a line ending in `\n`.

1. In `loop()`, check `Serial.available()` to see if bytes have arrived.
2. Read one line with `Serial.readStringUntil('\n')` and `trim()` it.
3. `on` turns the LED on and prints `LED ON`. `off` turns it off and prints `LED OFF`.

The check types `on` at 1 s and `off` at 2.5 s.
hints: Only read when Serial.available() > 0, otherwise you wait for text that is not there.
String cmd = Serial.readStringUntil('\n'); cmd.trim(); then compare with cmd == "on".

if (Serial.available() > 0) { String cmd = Serial.readStringUntil('\n'); cmd.trim(); if (cmd == "on") { digitalWrite(LED_PIN, HIGH); Serial.println("LED ON"); } else if (cmd == "off") { digitalWrite(LED_PIN, LOW); Serial.println("LED OFF"); } }
